newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in featureless trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. May Federal budget report, dealers said on Friday.
The U.S. Treasury will be releasing its monthly budget for May which is forecast to show a deficit of US$49.4 billion compared with a $93.94 billion surplus reported in April.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the Federal Budget data for fresh clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact here as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions for the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend, Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
